description: Distribute balls with overlaps until a target porosity is achieved. Ball positions and radii are drawn from uniform distributions (or Gaussian/FISH distributions). Significant ball overlaps will likely result from this operation. This command contrasts with ball generate where balls are generated without overlap.

python_sdk_alternative.workaround: itasca.command('ball distribute ...') - no Python SDK equivalent for porosity-based distribution with overlaps

notes: Bin keywords: radius <radlow> <radhi>: Radius range for uniform distribution (default: 1.0 1.0); gauss <f>: Use Gaussian distribution with mean=(radlow+radhi)/2, std=(radhi-radlow)/2. Optional f (default 0.1) sets minimum radius; fish-distribution <function_name> <args...>: Use FISH function to generate radii. Cannot be used with gauss or radius; volume-fraction <f>: Volume fraction for this bin (all bins must sum to 1.0); group <s> slot <slot>: Assign generated balls to group

description.6.0: Specify the distributional properties of bin i . Any number of distributions with radii ranges, volume fractions, and distributional types can be specified. The volume fractions of all distributions must sum to 1. Options: fish-distribution <s>a...a: The ball radii are drawn from the distribution represented by the FISH function s . Function arguments can be specified as though no function arguments are required. The FISH function must return a floating point value that is the ball radius. A FISH distribution cannot be specified with the gauss or radius keywords.; gauss [<f>]: Specify that the ball radii are chosen from a Gaussian distribution with mean value ( fradlow + fradhi )/2 and standard deviation ( fradhi - fradlow )/2. The optional f (default 0.1), multiplied by fradlow , constitutes the minimum radius allowed.; group <s>[slot <slot>] ...: Specify that generated balls are given group name s at slot slot . description.6.0: Ball will fully fall within this box, such that they will not overlap the box faces or edges. If the y,z -boundaries are omitted, they will be taken as equal to the x -boundaries. If the z -boundaries are omitted, they will be taken equal to the y -boundaries. By default, the box is the model domain.
description.7.0: Ball will fully fall within this box, such that they will not overlap the box faces or edges. If the y,z -boundaries are omitted, they will be taken as equal to the \(x\) -boundaries. If the \(z\) -boundaries are omitted, they will be taken equal to the \(y\) -boundaries. By default, the box is the model domain.

keywords.name: number-bins
keywords.description: Number of distributions used to generate the assembly.

keywords.name: porosity
keywords.description: The final porosity is set to f . By default, f = {0.16 in 2D; 0.359 in 3D} corresponding to the porosity for a tight, mono-disperse packing of {disks in 2D; spheres in 3D}.

keywords.name: resolution
keywords.description: Optional resolution that can be used as a multiplicative factor of the radii of each ball generated. By default, f = 1.0.

keywords.name: fish-distribution
keywords.description: The ball radii are drawn from the distribution represented by the FISH function s. Function arguments can be specified as though no function arguments are required. The FISH function must return a floating point value that is the ball radius.

keywords.name: gauss
keywords.description: Specify that the ball radii are chosen from a Gaussian distribution with mean value (fradlow + fradhi)/2 and standard deviation (fradhi - fradlow)/2. The optional f (default 0.1), multiplied by fradlow, constitutes the minimum radius allowed.

keywords.name: group
keywords.description: Specify that generated balls are given group name s at slot slot. If the slot keyword is not specified, then the group name is assigned to the slot Default.

keywords.name: radius
keywords.description: Specify the radius range to be used during generation. If fradhi is not specified, then fradhi = fradlow. By default fradhi = fradlow = 1.0. Cannot be given with the fish-distribution keyword.

examples.description: Distribute balls with radius 1.0-1.6 to achieve 30% porosity (allows overlaps)

examples.command: ball distribute number-bins 2 bin 1 radius 0.5 1.0 volume-fraction 0.6 bin 2 radius 1.0 1.5 volume-fraction 0.4 porosity 0.35
examples.description: Two size distributions: 60% small balls (0.5-1.0), 40% large balls (1.0-1.5)

examples.command: ball distribute radius 1.0 1.5 gauss 0.1 porosity 0.32 box -10 10 -10 10 -5 5
examples.description: Gaussian distribution in specified box region

examples.command: ball distribute number-bins 1 bin 1 radius 0.8 1.2 group 'layer1' volume-fraction 1.0 porosity 0.38

notes: This command embeds reference figures that are not captured in this text corpus. Figures are PNGs under <doc-root>/_images/ (doc-root sits beside the engine install, e.g. C:/Program Files/Itasca/<product>/exe64/doc); read them directly.
